subject: Immediate: Medisys 429 spike — org/project quota mapping error
messages:
From: Carla Santos <carla@medisyshealth.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@medisyshealth.com
Date: Mon, 26 Oct 2026 09:17:12 -0700
Subject: URGENT: 429 spikes causing outages in production

Connor / Marissa,

We started seeing a massive uptick in 429 responses across our production cluster starting ~03:00 PDT. Frontline shows request failures for our document-processing pipelines (batch inference jobs and realtime API calls). Error rates climbed to ~18% and several customer-facing endpoints timed out when clients retried aggressively. We've attached a small sample of the logs and a screenshot from our dashboard.

Impact: multiple customers reporting failed ingestion and slow UX; sales/legal are now involved.

We've tried backing off client retries but the spike continues. Could this be a quota or tiering mismatch on your side? Previously you made the per-project tiering change for onboarding — maybe something mapped incorrectly.

Attachments: support_logs_20261026.zip (log bundle)

Please escalate; we need a hot fix and confirmation of the root cause.

— Carla
VP Engineering, Medisys Health

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 26 Oct 2026 09:30:05 -0700
Subject: Fwd: URGENT: 429 spikes causing outages in production

Marissa / Aditya — passing this along. TL;DR: customer is seeing a 429 surge that looks like a quota cap rather than a model bug (high 429% + simultaneous requests across many projects). First assessment: the new onboarding script that sets project->org tier mapping may have assigned several Medisys projects to the "starter" tier instead of "enterprise". Starter tier has a per-project RPS ceiling that can trigger a retry storm when client-side backoff is poor.

Immediate asks:
- Aditya: can you confirm current quota for Medisys project IDs in infra and temporarily bump the project quota to match their expected enterprise tier (roll-forward + telemetry to monitor)?
- Marissa: please coordinate a short-lived routing rule to prefer their requests to the dedicated pool (if available) to reduce 429s while we validate mapping.
- I will notify the customer of the temporary mitigation and ask them to hold retries for 5 minutes while we validate.

Notes on mitigation sequence (short):
1) Verify mapping in onboarding logs for the affected tenant IDs.
2) If mapping incorrect, patch the mapping service and roll a canary.
3) Temporarily increase project quota for the affected project(s) (30m window) and monitor.
4) Add a short-term server-side retry-suppress header (X-Redwood-Suppress-Retry: 1) response so well-behaved clients don't amplify the storm.

Aditya — please update this thread with the exact project IDs and quota numbers you changed. I'll loop in Naomi if we need an executive credit/contract concession.

— Connor

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Carla Santos <carla@medisyshealth.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@medisyshealth.com
Date: Mon, 26 Oct 2026 10:05:43 -0700
Subject: Re: URGENT: 429 spikes causing outages in production

Carla — thanks for the signal and logs. We're confirming now. Quick update:

What we found: onboarding mapping script (v2.3.1) applied an incorrect tier label to three Medisys project IDs (project-8374, project-8375, project-8376). The projects were assigned "starter" instead of "enterprise" due to a missing lookup for the enterprise account tag.

Actions taken (10:00–10:03 PDT):
- Increased per-project RPS for project-8374/5/6 from 60 RPS -> 600 RPS (temporary 45-minute window).
- Enabled routing preference to dedicated pool for those projects.
- Returned a response header X-Redwood-Suppress-Retry for 5 minutes to discourage aggressive client retry loops.

We attached the log bundle and a short patch for the mapping service. Please smoke-test now.

Attachments: support_logs_20261026.zip

Carla — can you run a quick set of POST requests to confirm behavior? If you still see 429s after 10:15 PDT, we will open an infra emergency and keep a live bridge.

— Aditya, SRE

From: Carla Santos <carla@medisyshealth.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@medisyshealth.com
Date: Tue, 27 Oct 2026 08:42:11 -0700
Subject: Re: URGENT: 429 spikes causing outages in production

Hi Aditya / Connor —

Thanks — we ran validation tests at ~10:30 PDT after your change. 429 rates dropped dramatically (from ~18% to ~1.4%) and the UX returned for most flows. A subset of longer-running batch jobs still observed timeouts (likely from client retry queues). We can confirm the temporary bump fixed the immediate service impact.

Request for next steps:
- We need a post-mortem RCA on why the onboarding script assigned the wrong tier.
- We expect a permanent fix (patch + test) and an automated audit to prevent future mapping regressions.
- Please confirm what remediation/credit we should expect — procurement is cc'd.

I'll keep monitoring and will escalate internally if anything recurs.

— Carla

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Carla Santos <carla@medisyshealth.com>, procurement@medisyshealth.com
Date: Thu, 28 Oct 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-incident: Medisys 429 spike — RCA & next steps

Team / Carla,

Follow-up and plan after the last 48 hours: incident contained, customer service restored. Summary: onboarding script v2.3.1 failed to map three Medisys projects to the enterprise tier due to a missing enterprise-tag lookup, which left them on the starter tier with a low per-project RPS ceiling. This, combined with aggressive client retries, created a retry storm and large number of 429s.

Immediate remediation we completed:
- Corrected mapping records for project-8374/5/6 and deployed a fix to mapping service (canary + full rollout).
- Temporarily increased project quotas and routed traffic to dedicated pool until the canary validated.
- Inserted X-Redwood-Suppress-Retry header for 10m during the peak to mitigate amplification.

Action items and owners:
- Marissa: add unit and integration tests for tenant-tag lookup and add a nightly audit that validates project->tier assignments (due: 2026-11-04).
- Aditya: produce a patch (rfc-quota-change.patch.diff attached) for mapping service and ship a 1.2.2 release; include telemetry to alert when a project has a starter quota but enterprise spend/usage pattern (due: 2026-10-31).
- Connor / Naomi: propose customer remediation (one-month credit + SLO commitment) and draft a customer-facing RCA (due: 2026-11-02).

Carla — we'll follow up with a formal RCA doc and a proposed credit + SLO package. We are very sorry for the disruption and will treat this as a priority to avoid recurrence.

Related links: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/companies/medisys | https://drive.redwood.com/incident/medisys-20261026/logs

Attachments: rfc-quota-change.patch.diff

— Connor
